## The BPA Lab

The **Business Process Automation Lab (BPA Lab)** is an ongoing project at **TH Köln (University of Applied Sciences)** that supports research and teaching in the field of business process automation and analytics. It is run within the area of Information and Process Management at the Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering Sciences and serves as a platform on which lecturers and students can study and extend selected concepts and technologies of business process automation.

As a *demonstration and research platform*, the BPA Lab provides an environment in which bachelor's and master's theses as well as smaller research projects can address questions around process automation and process analysis — for example regarding data architectures, process mining, or the human–system interfaces of business processes. The projects collected in [Chapter 6](chapter06-projects.qmd) illustrate the range of work that has been carried out on this basis.

As a *teaching* platform, the BPA Lab is used to support teaching in the field of business process automation and analysis. It offers students a tangible end-to-end scenario in which processes can be modelled, implemented in a BPMS, executed against physical hardware, and analysed using the resulting data. The didactic rationale and an early evaluation of this approach are documented in the project's first SoTL publication ([Chapter 6](chapter06-projects.qmd#sec-sotl-cos1326)).

## Physical setup

This book documents the fictional **business scenario**, the **physical and software implementation** and an overview of the projects conducted so far in the BPA Lab.

![BPA Lab — Conceptual Architecture](images/Conceptional_Architecture.png){#fig-concept fig-align="center"}


The lab combines **software components** (Business Process Management Systems, Robotic Process Automation, Process Mining) with **hardware components** (a Fischertechnik Industry 4.0 factory, a Fischertechnik warehouse robot, and IoT devices) to simulate the production and logistics processes of a bicycle manufacturer.

## About this book

This book aims to provide:

1. A **high-level overview** of the BPA Lab and its goals.
2. A **description of the business scenario** — the end-to-end ordering, manufacturing, and shipment process implemented in the lab.
3. A **description of the software and system architecture** and the design decisions taken along the way.
4. A **collection of projects** that have been carried out using the BPA Lab.

It is structured as follows:

1. **Introduction:** Motivation, goals, and scope of the BPA Lab.
2. **Solution overview:** The three architectural layers — controllers, process applications, workflow engine.
3. **Business scenario:** The end-to-end bicycle ordering, manufacturing, and shipment process, broken down into its sub-processes (order management, production control, purchasing, manufacturing, shipment, warehouse operations).
4. **Data and data sources:** Data model, data flows, and persistence in the BPA Lab.
5. **Software architecture:** Requirements, a C4 view of the system, and the architecture decisions taken so far.
6. **Projects:** Research and teaching projects conducted using the BPA Lab.

The appendices contain:

- **Appendix A:** Overview of related components and sister repositories.
- **Appendix B:** A glossary of key terms.
- **References:** All cited literature.

## Who this book is for

This book is written for:

- **Students** working on bachelor's or master's projects inside the BPA Lab.
- **Lecturers and researchers** who are interested in teaching business process automation with a tangible reference system.
- **Practitioners** looking for a concepts on combining a BPMS, IoT hardware, and process mining.

## Source code and related repositories

The implementation of the demonstration factory is maintained as a separate repository: [bpa_lab_demonstration_factory](https://github.com/BpaLabTHCologne/bpa_lab_demonstration_factory).

Documentation for student component projects is available in the wiki of [bpa_lab_student_docs](https://github.com/BpaLabTHCologne/bpa_lab_student_docs/wiki).
